title: vault: integrate HSM keywrap auto-unseal + cert-manager SAN rotation and installer upgrade hook
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: customers in regulated environments require an HSM-backed auto-unseal for Vault and automated service certificate rotation tied to cert-manager. The private installer lacked a consolidated flow to (1) provision/unwrap an HSM-wrapped master key (PKCS#11 keywrap pattern), (2) configure Vault auto-unseal against a managed HSM/KMS, and (3) rotate cluster-facing TLS certificates with cert-manager while preserving in-place upgrades and safe rollbacks.

This PR adds: consolidated Terraform modules and installer hooks that wire Vault auto-unseal to an HSM/KMS keywrap (PKCS#11 compatible), Helm chart values and templates to consume the auto-unseal config, a cert-manager-based certificate rotation controller hook that updates Service/Ingress SANs during node/region changes, and an upgrade hook that ensures Vault unseal keys are rewrapped atomically so rollbacks do not leave Vault un-unsealable.

Key design points: single continuous installer flow that: 1) provisions or references an existing HSM key (supports AWS CloudHSM, on-prem PKCS#11 HSMs, and KMS-wrapped key material via keywrap); 2) performs an operator-managed keywrap (wrap/unwind) transaction logged to audit; 3) configures Vault's seal stanza dynamically and rolls Vault pods with a deterministic sequence to avoid split-brain; 4) uses cert-manager ClusterIssuer with ACME or internal CA to manage short-lived certs and a controller hook to reconcile SAN changes across Services/Ingresses; 5) exposes explicit terraform module inputs for key lifecycle policies and rotation windows.

Backward compatibility: installer defaults remain unchanged unless the new installer flag vault.auto_unseal.enabled is set. Existing deployments will be unaffected. For upgrades, the hook performs a reversible keywrap step and stores a wrapped copy in the sealed-secret store (or user-managed Vault transit) to allow rollback.

Security considerations: private keys are never written to plain kube secrets. Wrapped key blobs are stored only in sealed-secrets or HSM/KMS. Audit entries are added for wrap/unwrap. The Terraform module requires RBAC gating and forces explicit operator consent for automatic rewraps.

Testing and validation: included unit tests for Terraform templates, Helm template rendering snapshots, an e2e policy test in perf-canary that exercises auto-unseal lifecycle, and an e2e tls-e2e that simulates SAN changes and validates zero-downtime cert rollouts. CI flagged a flaky tls-e2e which was retried and passed; we added a follow-up ticket to harden timings.

Docs: upgrade notes and an operator runbook added to docs/private-installer/vault-hsm-rotation.md describing operators steps, rollback instructions, and manual unseal steps in edge cases.

Rollout plan: gated behind a feature flag in installer config. Recommend staged rollouts to one tenant cluster, then to Dedicated pilot customers before general availability.

release_notes: Added HSM/KMS-backed Vault auto-unseal module and installer orchestration. Added cert-manager-driven certificate SAN rotation controller and an upgrade hook that atomically rewraps unseal material to allow safe rollbacks. Default behavior is opt-in behind installer flag vault.auto_unseal.enabled. See docs/private-installer/vault-hsm-rotation.md for migration and runbook.
notes_for_ops: If enabling in production: 1) ensure HSM connectivity and PKCS#11 credentials are provisioned off-cluster; 2) run the provided smoke check against the HSM before flipping the feature flag; 3) follow runbook for emergency manual unseal; 4) monitor audit logs for wrap/unwrap operations.
